subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for DeltaSecure
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@deltasecure.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery call recap & next steps — Dedicated capacity evaluation

Hi Rafael / Marissa,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the thorough walk-through of Redwood's Dedicated offering. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying items so we're aligned on next steps.

Summary of pain points
- Model throughput unpredictability: our current infra (self-hosted on GCP preemptible VMs + occasional burst to managed endpoints) spikes during batch re-runs and nightly enrichment jobs, causing timeouts and backoff retries.
- Data isolation & compliance: we handle regulated user PII and need hardware-level isolation and auditability for certain workloads.
- Cost predictability: finance needs a committed cost profile for next 12 months; current pay-as-you-go is spiky and hard to forecast.

Current stack
- Models: mix of open Llama-derivatives and a few fine-tuned encoder-decoder models for extraction.
- Infra: GCP (preemptible + autoscaling), Kafka for ingestion, Redis for caches.
- Orchestration: Argo + Terraform for infra-as-code.

Success criteria (what will make a Dedicated deployment a success)
1) Consistent TPS and P99 latency within our SLA: target 150 TPS sustained for the most common CPU-bound prompt with 95th latency < 200ms for our live endpoint.
2) Isolation and controls: network segregation (VPC), customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), and audit logs we can push into our SIEM.
3) Autoscale/burst behavior: ability to sustain brief bursts up to 400 TPS for windows up to 5 minutes without dropped requests.
4) Cost: committed monthly spend with predictable unit cost that beats our current average per-1000-token cost by >=20%.

Clarifying questions (for sizing & proposal)
- Can you confirm how Redwood Dedicated defines "TPS" for mixed batch vs interactive workloads? Is it per-VM or per-pool?
- Do you support HW isolation (dedicated GPUs per tenant) vs shared multi-tenant pools?
- What are typical cold-starts for model loading for our model sizes (7B–13B) on your default runtime?

Next steps we discussed
1) Redwood to send an initial sizing + committment proposal with 30/60/90-day rollout options.
2) DeltaSecure to share traffic profiles (15-minute bins for last 30 days) + retention/compliance controls documentation (by EOD Friday).
3) Schedule follow-up to review proposal and technical runbook — target next Tuesday.

Attachments: sending an infra summary and example traffic profile in a follow-up (PDF).

Thanks,
Alex
Product Ops — DeltaSecure
alex.chen@deltasecure.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@deltasecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap & next steps — Dedicated capacity evaluation

Alex — really helpful summary, thank you. Glad we're aligned on the core success criteria. A few quick answers and what we'll deliver next: 

- TPS definition: in Redwood Dedicated we report effective TPS at the pool level (requests served/sec across the GPU pool) and per-model concurrency. For mixed batch/interactive we present both sustained TPS and burst headroom; the proposal will include both numbers.
- Isolation options: we support both multi-tenant pools with strict tenant isolation and fully dedicated GPU pools (reserved capacity) for customers that require physical isolation. We can size a dedicated pool for DeltaSecure.
- Cold-starts: for 7B–13B models on the optimized runtime you should expect model load times ~30–90s depending on quantization and KV cache warming; we'll outline preload + warmup strategies to minimize impact.

Deliverables by end of day Wednesday (our side)
1) Draft proposal (attached to Marissa's email) with a 3-tier sizing (baseline, scale, burst) including estimated monthly cost and expected sustained/burst TPS.
2) Technical runbook checklist (networking, KMS, audit log sinks, model onboarding requirements).
3) A short SLA/RTO note describing isolation guarantees and fallback policies.

Can you please confirm the traffic profile file you'll share will include: 15-minute bins, typical payload size (avg tokens per request), and percent of requests that are interactive vs batch? That will help us nail the sizing.

Also proposing a 30-minute technical review on Tue Jul 7 at 10:00am PT — let me know if that works and I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@deltasecure.com>, Priya Rao <pri.rao@deltasecure.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap & next steps — Dedicated capacity evaluation

Hi Alex / Priya — following up with the draft proposal and infra checklist we discussed. Attaching the two docs to this thread for review: redwood-proposal-draft-v1.pdf (contains baseline/scale/burst sizing + pricing bands) and deltasecure-infra-summary.pdf (summary of items we need from your infra team).

Quick highlights from the proposal: 
- Baseline pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs, expected sustained throughput ~160 TPS for your most common interactive endpoint; estimated monthly committed spend $38,000.
- Scale pool: add 8 GPUs for higher concurrency and redundancy; sustained ~320 TPS.
- Burst policy: automatic burst to a reserved burst tranche that can absorb short 5-minute spikes up to ~420 TPS with graceful degrade rules applied.
- Isolation: option for fully reserved GPU pool with dedicated hardware, VPC peering, and KMS/HSM integration documented.

Action items for DeltaSecure
- Share traffic bins + token sizes and confirm retention / PII controls (reply here).
- Confirm interest in dedicated hardware vs multi-tenant isolated pool so we can lock down pricing.
- Accept calendar invite for Tue Jul 7 10:00am PT (sent) or propose alternate slot.

If you want, we can run a proof-of-concept for a single model (7B) for 2 weeks to validate latency and scaling before committing to a 3/6/12 month capacity contract. POC scope and success criteria are in the proposal appendix.

Thanks — looking forward to the traffic file.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-proposal-draft-v1.pdf, deltasecure-infra-summary.pdf
